sections.heading: Daily report
paragraphs: Two meaningful product changes landed after the October 20 brief and before the October 21 morning cutoff.

Thingamajob’s public experience changed substantially: the historical demo was replaced as the primary interaction by the unfinished Text/URL/File evaluator. It uses James’s canonical career evidence, clearly labels itself as a working prototype, retains detailed assessments privately, preserves the public/protected boundary, and uses the existing controlled same-origin evaluation path.

The theme menu was also optimized without redesigning it. Nine first-open lazy SVG requests were consolidated into one content-hashed, immutably cached SVG sprite while preserving the approved artwork, labels, keyboard/focus behavior, forced-colors behavior and accessibility.
Those are the October 21 brief’s changes.
The Buildometer/homepage layout and deployment-grid work performed later on October 21 did not exist at this cutoff and belongs to the next brief.

sections.heading: Daily report
paragraphs: Because no October 18 brief had been published, this brief covers the meaningful change since the last successful publication.

Mobile startup work had been tightened and Buildometer had become a real evidence-backed dashboard with its approved T₀ baseline. The homepage teaser and durable daily development reports were in place, and the older Scrum history had been reconstructed.

On October 19 itself, the production scheduler was connected to the existing Scrum workflow dispatch, Cloudflare’s empty POST behavior was handled, the required runtime secret was bound correctly, and the Daily Scrum Brief successfully published after those corrections.
The meaningful story was Buildometer, durable reporting, and getting the automation genuinely operational.

sections.heading: Daily report
paragraphs: The approved public site was reconciled back onto `main` without dragging protected Thingamajob server/API/TEST implementation into the public application.

The public workflow was decoupled from the protected implementation, the build passed, and the public demo made no protected API requests. There was intentionally no new visual/product feature in that baseline.

Immediately afterward, the Daily Scrum Brief and permanent Product Journal machinery were activated. October 16 was preserved as the initial history entry, dated journal routes were established, Cloudflare publication verification was wired in, and the daily 10 AM Eastern schedule was established.
This day’s actual story was public/protected reconciliation plus journal automation.

sections.heading: Daily report
paragraphs: Client #1 proved exception-based review: clean directly supported facts could be established automatically, routine discrepancies could be resolved without unnecessary owner intervention, and the false-positive questions had been eliminated. No human-required questions remained.
Protected TEST presented a usable résumé assembly with provenance, correction history and diagnostics. JD evaluation and sealed-benchmark comparison had not started.

On the public site, Home and the case study shared one Thingamajob component. The four candidate/job evidence outcomes were established; the corrected homepage presentation, texture/depth work and living-theme shadows were live; five reviewed responsive artwork slides had replaced the temporary designs; Creative Town remained unchanged; AVIF/WebP delivery was live; production had returned to perfect Lighthouse scores.
The next explicit gate was the sealed benchmark comparison. Real JD evaluation would follow only if that comparison held up.

sections.heading: Daily report
paragraphs: Thingamajob moved from concept toward protected application infrastructure. Trusted workspace ownership and protected TEST access were established alongside private storage, evidence intake and owner-only assertion review.
The trust boundary mattered: remote TEST ownership could not simply accept browser-supplied identity, and private-storage readiness had to be established before the workflow could be trusted.
